English[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
A Associação Open Finance é responsável por criar padrões e especificações necessárias para atender aos requisitos e obrigações da Legislação do Open Finance do Brasil, conforme originalmente delineado pelo
Banco Central do Brasil
e Conselho Monetário Nacional. É possível que alguns dos elementos deste documento estejam sujeitos a direitos autorais ou patenteados. A Associação Open Finance não se responsabiliza pela identificação de qualquer ou todos esses direitos.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
O Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil (FAPI-BR) consiste nas seguintes partes:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 2.2.1[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Open Finance Brasil Dynamic Client Registration Profile 2.1.0[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
O Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil é uma implementação do perfil
FAPI-1-Advanced
que fornece diretrizes de implementação específicas para segurança e interoperabilidade que devem ser aplicadas as APIs expostas no ecossistema do Open Finance Brasil. O Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil é um subconjunto do perfil
FAPI-1-Advanced
, no entanto esse subconjunto não se refere a retirada de mecanismos de segurança do perfil original e sim a obrigatoriedade de utilização de determinadas características do mesmo visando a facilitação da interoperabilidade entre as instituições financeiras.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Este perfil descreve as capacidades e os recursos de segurança que devem ser oferecidos por servidores e clientes que são necessários para o ecossistema do Open Finance Brasil, definindo as medidas para mitigar ou endereçar:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
ataques que abordam considerações de privacidade identificadas na cláusula 9.1 de
FAPI-1-Advanced
.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
o requisito de concessão de acesso granular a recursos, com vistas à minimização de dados;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
o requisito de informar sobre o contexto da autenticação do usuário (claim Authentication Context Request - acr) que foi realizada por um Provedor OpenID, com vistas a favorecer o adequado gerenciamento do risco decorrente do acesso do usuário;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Este perfil também especifica o método para os aplicativos:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
obterem de maneira segura os tokens OAuth necessários para acesso a dados críticos de acordo com os requisitos do
Open Finance Brasil
;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
utilizarem o OpenID Connect para identificação do usuário do Open Finance; e[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
utilizarem o OpenID Connect para afirmar a identidade do cliente.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Embora seja possível codificar do início um servidor de autorização que atenda ao Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil, o público alvo desta especificação são os provedores que já possuem uma implementação certificada do
FAPI-1-Advanced
e desejam realizar as adequações necessárias para obter a certificação para o Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Estas partes são destinados a serem usados com
RFC6749
,
RFC6750
,
RFC7636
,
OIDC
,
FAPI-1-Baseline
e
FAPI-1-Advanced
.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
As palavras-chave "deve" (shall), "não deve" (shall not), "deveria" (should), "não deveria" (should not) e "pode" (may) presentes nesse documento devem ser interpretadas conforme as diretrizes descritas em
ISODIR2
observando seguinte equivalência:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
"deve" => equivalente ao termo "shall" e expressa um requerimento definido no documento (nas traduções é similar ao termo "must", que pode denotar um requerimento externo ao documento);[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
"não deve" => equivalente ao termo "shall not" e também expressa um requerimento definido no documento;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
"deveria" e "não deveria"=> equivalente ao termo "should" e "should not" e expressa uma recomendação[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
"pode" => equivalente ao termo "may" indica uma permissão[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Estas palavras-chave não são usadas como termos de dicionário, de modo que qualquer ocorrência deles deve ser interpretada como palavras-chave e não devem ser interpretados com seus significados de linguagem natural.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1

O consentimento é um objeto de negócio fundamental, fortemente vinculado aos artefatos de segurança (refresh e access tokens). No entanto, seu ciclo de vida deve ser gerenciado de forma independente, através de sua própria máquina de estados. As especificações funcionais da API publicadas pelo Open Finance Brasil definem as transições de estado, os comportamentos esperados e as condições de erro dos recursos REST protegidos por este perfil, garantindo o controle adequado sobre o ciclo de vida do consentimento.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1

deve, sempre que possível, revogar e cessar o uso de refresh e de access tokens vinculados a um consentimento (Consent Resource Object) que foi excluído;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
deve excluir consentimentos (Consent Resource Objects) que estão expirados.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1

The Open Finance Brasil Security Profile (FAPI-BR) consists of the following parts:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1

The Open Finance Brasil Security Profile is an implementation of the
FAPI-1-Advanced
profile that provides specific implementation guidelines for security and interoperability that shall be applied to APIs exposed in the Open Finance Brasil ecosystem. The Open Finance Brasil Security Profile is a subset of the
FAPI-1-Advanced
; however, this subset does not refer to the removal of security mechanisms from the original profile, but rather to the mandatory use of certain characteristics of that profile in order to facilitate interoperability among financial institutions.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
This profile describes the capabilities and security features that shall be provided by servers and clients that are necessary for the Open Finance Brasil ecosystem, defining measures to mitigate or address:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
attacks that address privacy considerations identified in clause 9.1 of
FAPI-1-Advanced
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
the requirement to support fine-grained access to resources, for data minimisation purposes;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
the requirement to convey the Authentication Context Request (acr claim) that was performed by an OpenID Provider, in order to enable appropriate risk management arising from user access.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
This profile also specifies the method for applications to:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
obtain the OAuth tokens in an appropriately secure manner for access to critical data in a manner that meets the requirements of
Open Finance Brasil
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
use OpenID Connect to identify the Open Finance user; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
use OpenID Connect to assert the identity of the client.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1

Note 1:
Protected resource endpoints are those belonging to product APIs that require authentication, such as /consents, /resources, /accounts, and /payments, among others. Security endpoints (such as /authorize, /token, /introspect, /revocation, and /register) and endpoints of open data APIs do not fall into this category.
Note 2:
Authorization servers that enforce one-time use of

values must ensure the enforcement takes place at the point of authorization, not at the point of loading an authorization page.  This requirement prevents behaviors such as URL preloads by user agents or duplicated calls (for example, simultaneous requests to the browser and the OP application) from causing improper invalidation of the
request_uri

for the encryption of the id_token, a key of type "enc" available in the JWKS informed in the jwks_uri parameter of the client registration (DCR) must be used. shall always include the acr claim in the id_token. The value of the acr claim must be one of the allowed values as defined in the section Authentication contexts (acr);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1

This profile defines
urn:brasil:openbanking:loa2 (LoA2)
and
urn:brasil:openbanking:loa3 (LoA3)

LoA2: authentication mechanism using a single factor;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
LoA3: authentication mechanism using multiple authentication factors.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
The following guidance must be observed for the authentication mechanism of Open Finance Brasil APIs:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
In accordance with Art. 17 of Joint Resolution no. 01, institutions must adopt procedures and controls for client authentication compatible with those applicable to access to their electronic service channels.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
In accordance with the regulation in force, it is suggested that:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
For user authentication in authorisations to access data sharing APIs, Authorization Servers should adopt, at least, a method compatible with LoA2; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
For user authentication in authorisations to access payment initiation or service/product contracting APIs, Authorization Servers should adopt an authentication method compatible with LoA3 or higher.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
In all cases, the adoption of a more rigorous authentication mechanism (LoA3 or higher) is at the discretion of the transmitting/account-holding institution, according to its risk assessment and in a manner compatible with the mechanisms usually employed.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Additional clarification on authentication factors[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Authentication factors are:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Something you know, such as a password or secret phrase;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Something you have, such as a token, smartcard or device;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Something you are, that is, authentication conditioned on the presentation of a physical characteristic that is exclusively yours, such as biometric validation.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
To perform multi-factor authentication (MFA), it is necessary that the user presents at least two different factors from those listed above. A single factor used more than once – for example, presenting two passwords that the user knows – cannot be accepted as MFA.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1

JWS standard defined in RFC7515 shall be adopted to ensure integrity and non-repudiation of information processed in sensitive API's (message sign requirement is indicated at API's documentation/swagger), which includes:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Header (JSON Object Signing and Encryption - JOSE Header), which defines the algorithm used and includes information about the public key or certificate that can be used to validate the signature;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Payload (JWS Payload): the content itself as detailed in the API specification;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Digital signature (JWS Signature): digital signature, performed according to the header parameters.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Each of the elements above must be encoded using the Base64url pattern
RFC4648
and, once this is done, the elements must be concatenated with "." (JWS Compact Serialization method, as defined in
RFC7515
).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
The payload of signed messages (request JWT and response JWT) shall include the following claims as defined in
RFC7519
:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
aud (in the JWT request): the Resource Provider (e.g. the institution holding the account) must validate whether the value of the aud field matches the endpoint being triggered;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
aud (in the JWT response): the API client (e.g. initiating institution) shall validate whether the value of the aud field matches its own organisationId listed in the directory;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
iss (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the receiver of the message shall validate whether the value of the iss field matches the organisationId of the sender;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
jti (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the value of the jti field shall be filled with the UUID defined by the institution in accordance with [RFC4122] using version 4;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
iat (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the value of the iat field shall be filled with the message generation time and in accordance with the standard established in
RFC7519
for the NumericDate format.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
cty (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the value of the cty field shall be filled in; in the normal case in which nested signing or encryption operations are not employed, the use of this header parameter is not recommended. In the case that nested signing or encryption is employed, this header parameter must be present; in this case, the value must be "JWT", to indicate that a nested JWT is carried in this JWT. While media type names are not case sensitive, it is recommended that "JWT" always be spelled using uppercase characters for compatibility with legacy implementations.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
The HTTP content-type of requests and responses with JWS messages shall be defined as: "application/jwt".[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
The JOSE header must contain the following attributes:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
alg - shall be filled with the value PS256";[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
kid - shall be filled with the key identifier value used for the signature;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
typ - shall be filled with the value JWT.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
In case of error in signature validation by Resource Provider the API provider shall return HTTP error message with status code 400 and the ResponseError content shall include, in the code property, the content BAD_SIGNATURE.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Errors in validating the signed messages received by the client application (e.g. payment initiator) must be logged and the Resource Provider (e.g. account-holding institution) must be notified.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
The receiver shall validate the consistency of the JWS message's digital signature exclusively based on the information obtained from the directory, that is, based on the keys published in the institution's JWKS in the directory.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Signatures must be performed using the digital signature certificate specified in the
Open Finance Brazil Certificates Standard
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
the iat claim must be numeric in Unix Time format GMT+0 with a tolerance of +/- 60 seconds;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
the jti claim must be unique for a clientId within a time frame of 86,400 seconds (24h), and cannot be reused within this period. In case of reuse, the HTTP error code 403 shall be return. Any other case must follow RFC 6749 instructions in item 5.2.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
For JWS, both clients and authorization servers shall use the PS256 algorithm.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
For JWE, both clients and authorization servers shall use RSA-OAEP with A256GCM.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
For TLS, Authentication Server endpoints and Resource Server endpoints used directly by the client:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall support TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall support TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
The "TLS Session Resumption" and "TLS Renegotiation" features shall be disabled.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Existing mechanisms for appropriately managing access to resources defined in
RFC6749
are insufficient to meet the requirements of a modern data sharing ecosystem. Using static scope strings does not provide consumers with sufficient control and granularity to manage data sharing or resource management with third parties. Open Finance Brasil has elected to implement the parameterized scope (
FAPI-LIP
) associated with consent/binding APIs to manage fine-grained access to resources.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
This profile defines OAuth 2.0 dynamic scope "consent" as follows:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
string "consent", "recurring-consent" or "enrollment"; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
delimiter of a colon ":"; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Consent Resource Id returned by a successful creation of the resource to be granted (e.g. consent, recurring-consent, enrollment).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
In addition:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
the Consent Resource Id must include url safe characters only;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
the Consent Resource Id must be namespaced;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
the Consent Resource Id must have the properties of a
nonce
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Due to the characteristics of the Consent Resource Id and for ease of implementation, many institutions choose to use a UUIDv4 key as the Consent Resource Id; however, this is not a rule, and each institution may choose other methods provided that the rules presented above and also those defined in each API specification are respected.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Considering that the transmitting/account-holding institution is Banco Exemplo and that it is using UUIDv4 as the Consent Resource Id, the consents/recurring consents/device bindings created against this institution would have the following format, respectively:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
consent:urn:bancoexemplo:830ce3c6-e9e7-4800-ae93-3e9b29b470f1[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
recurring-consent:urn:bancoexemplo:c9a8a741-39a6-4014-bb75-e05934f9d711[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
enrollment:urn:bancoexemplo:eb093d20-ccc5-4242-a271-6658f6663712[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Consent is a fundamental business object, strongly linked to security artefacts (refresh and access tokens). However, its life cycle must be managed independently through its own state machine. The functional API specifications published by Open Finance Brasil define the state transitions, expected behaviours and error conditions for REST resources protected by this profile, ensuring appropriate control over the consent life cycle.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
The following requirements aim to instruct the behaviour of the Authorization Server (AS) in relation to the consent life cycle, ensuring that authorisation practices are aligned with regulatory expectations and the security of the entire ecosystem.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
In addition to the requirements outlined in Open Finance Brasil security provisions the Authorization Server:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall only issue refresh_tokens when linked to an active and valid consent;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Must not issue refresh_token when consent status is "CONSUMED" (for payment services);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Must issue an access_token through the grant_type client credentials when consent status is "CONSUMED" (for payment services);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
In an optimised journey, it shall issue refresh_tokens as long as at least one of the linked consents is active and valid.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall only share access to resources when presented access_token linked to an active consent and with the status "AUTHORISED“. For tokens generated with the scope: payments or recurring-payments, the status of the consent will not be validated.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
In the scenario of receiving an invalid token, status code 401 should be returned.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall revoke refresh tokens and, access tokens where aplicable, when the linked Consent Resource is deleted;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
In an optimised journey, it shall perform the revocation of refresh_tokens and access_tokens only if both linked consents are revoked.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall ensure access tokens are issued with sufficient scope necessary for access to data specified in the Permission element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall not reject an authorisation request requesting scopes broader than those necessary to access data specified in the Permissions element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
may reduce requested scope to a level sufficient to enable access to data resources specified in the Permissions element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall retain records on the consent history to allow the appropriate formation of audit trails in accordance with the regulation in force;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall return authentication failure and the return code access_denied in the error parameter (as specified in section 4.1.2.1 of
RFC6749
) if the CPF of the authenticated user is not the same as indicated in the loggedUser element of the related Consent Resource Object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall return authentication failure and the return code access_denied in the error parameter (as specified in section 4.1.2.1 of
RFC6749
) if the businessEntity element has not been populated in the related Consent Resource Object and the user has selected or authenticated using credentials related to a legal entity (business) account;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall condition the authentication or selection of legal entity (business) accounts to the consistency between the CNPJ related to the account(s) and the value present in the businessEntity element of the Consent Resource Object. In case of divergence, it shall return authentication failure and the return code access_denied in the error parameter (as specified in section 4.1.2.1 of
RFC6749
);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall issue a refresh_token with a validity period not shorter than the validity of the consent to which it is related, while respecting the other criteria above.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
Clarification note — refresh using a subset of scopes[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
For the purpose of interpreting the requirements of this section, when a
refresh_token
is associated with valid consent(s), the
Authorization Server
must maintain the set of scopes originally authorized by the customer as the reference.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
The request for, or issuance of, an
access_token
with a subset of scopes in a specific refresh operation may limit the token issued in that response, but must not permanently reduce the set of eligible scopes associated with the
refresh_token
, as long as the related consent(s) remain valid.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
In addition to the requirements outlined in Open Finance Brasil security provisions, the Confidential Client[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall revoke where possible and cease usage of refresh and access tokens that are bound to a Consent Resource that has been deleted;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1
shall delete Consent Resource that are expired;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.1

O Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil (FAPI-BR) consiste nas seguintes partes:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 2.2.0[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

O Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil é uma implementação do perfil
FAPI-1-Advanced
que fornece diretrizes de implementação específicas para segurança e interoperabilidade que devem ser aplicadas as APIs expostas no ecossistema do Open Finance Brasil. O Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil é um subconjunto do perfil
FAPI-1-Advanced
, no entanto esse subconjunto não se refere a retirada de mecanismos de segurança do perfil original e sim a obrigatoriedade de utilização de determinadas características do mesmo visando a facilitação da interoperabilidade entre as instituições financeiras.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Este perfil descreve as capacidades e os recursos de segurança que devem ser oferecidos por servidores e clientes que são necessários para o ecossistema do Open Finance Brasil, definindo as medidas para mitigar ou endereçar:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
ataques que abordam considerações de privacidade identificadas na cláusula 9.1 de
FAPI-1-Advanced
.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
o requisito de concessão de acesso granular a recursos, com vistas à minimização de dados;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
o requisito de informar sobre o contexto da autenticação do usuário (claim Authentication Context Request - acr) que foi realizada por um Provedor OpenID, com vistas a favorecer o adequado gerenciamento do risco decorrente do acesso do usuário;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Este perfil também especifica o método para os aplicativos:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
obterem de maneira segura os tokens OAuth necessários para acesso a dados críticos de acordo com os requisitos do
Open Finance Brasil
;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
utilizarem o OpenID Connect para identificação do usuário do Open Finance; e[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
utilizarem o OpenID Connect para afirmar a identidade do cliente.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Embora seja possível codificar do início um servidor de autorização que atenda ao Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil, o público alvo desta especificação são os provedores que já possuem uma implementação certificada do
FAPI-1-Advanced
e desejam realizar as adequações necessárias para obter a certificação para o Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

O consentimento é um objeto de negócio fundamental, fortemente vinculado aos artefatos de segurança (refresh e access tokens). No entanto, seu ciclo de vida deve ser gerenciado de forma independente, através de sua própria máquina de estados. As especificações funcionais da API publicadas pelo Open Finance Brasil definem as transições de estado, os comportamentos esperados e as condições de erro dos recursos REST protegidos por este perfil, garantindo o controle adequado sobre o ciclo de vida do consentimento.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Os requisitos a seguir visam instruir sobre o comportamento do Servidor de Autorização (AS) em relação ao ciclo de vida do consentimento, assegurando que as práticas de autorização estejam alinhadas com as expectativas normativas e a segurança de todo o ecossistema.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

The Open Finance Brasil Security Profile (FAPI-BR) consists of the following parts:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

The Open Finance Brasil Security Profile is an implementation of the
FAPI-1-Advanced
profile that provides specific implementation guidelines for security and interoperability that shall be applied to APIs exposed in the Open Finance Brasil ecosystem. The Open Finance Brasil Security Profile is a subset of the
FAPI-1-Advanced
; however, this subset does not refer to the removal of security mechanisms from the original profile, but rather to the mandatory use of certain characteristics of that profile in order to facilitate interoperability among financial institutions.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
This profile describes the capabilities and security features that shall be provided by servers and clients that are necessary for the Open Finance Brasil ecosystem, defining measures to mitigate or address:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
attacks that address privacy considerations identified in clause 9.1 of
FAPI-1-Advanced
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
the requirement to support fine-grained access to resources, for data minimisation purposes;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
the requirement to convey the Authentication Context Request (acr claim) that was performed by an OpenID Provider, in order to enable appropriate risk management arising from user access.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
This profile also specifies the method for applications to:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
obtain the OAuth tokens in an appropriately secure manner for access to critical data in a manner that meets the requirements of
Open Finance Brasil
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
use OpenID Connect to identify the Open Finance user; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
use OpenID Connect to assert the identity of the client.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

FAPI-1-Advanced
and wish to make the necessary adjustments to obtain certification for the Open Finance Brasil Security Profile.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

FAPI-1-Advanced
specification, and to support client management in the Open Finance Brasil ecosystem, the Open Finance Brasil Security Profile establishes that the Authorization Server shall support the provisions specified in clause 5.2.2 of
FAPI-1-Advanced
.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

should support the acr value "urn:brasil:openbanking:loa3" as defined in clause 5.1.1.1;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

may support

shall support the response_type value "code id_token";[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall not allow refresh token rotation;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall ensure that, in case of sharing the Authorization Server for other services, in addition to Open Finance, it does not disclose and/or allow the use of non-certified methods in the Open Finance environment;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall ensure that the settings disclosed to other participants through OpenID Discovery (indicated by the Well-Known file registered in the Directory) are restricted to the operating modes to which the institution has certified;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

shall issue refresh_tokens (JWT or opaque) with no expiration time in scenarios where they are required.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall enforce one-time use of

values at the authorization.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Note 1:
Protected resource endpoints are those belonging to product APIs that require authentication, such as /consents, /resources, /accounts, and /payments, among others. Security endpoints (such as /authorize, /token, /introspect, /revocation, and /register) and endpoints of open data APIs do not fall into this category.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Note 2:
Authorization servers that enforce one-time use of
request_uri
values must ensure the enforcement takes place at the point of authorization, not at the point of loading an authorization page.  This requirement prevents behaviors such as URL preloads by user agents or duplicated calls (for example, simultaneous requests to the browser and the OP application) from causing improper invalidation of the
request_uri

The Authorization Server shall support the provisions specified in clause 5.2.2.1 of
FAPI-1-Advanced
and, in addition, in order to meet specific requirements of the Open Finance Brasil Security Profile, it shall:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall encrypt the id_token in callback and token endpoint calls;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
for the encryption of the id_token, a key of type "enc" available in the JWKS informed in the jwks_uri parameter of the client registration (DCR) must be used. The kid of the key used for the id_token encryption must be indicated in the kid attribute of the JWT header;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall always include the acr claim in the id_token. The value of the acr claim must be one of the allowed values as defined in the section Authentication contexts (acr);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
The use of other headers to indicate the key used, such as x5u, x5c, jku or jkw, is prohibited as defined in clause 2 of
OIDC-Core
.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
This profile defines
urn:brasil:openbanking:loa2 (LoA2)
and
urn:brasil:openbanking:loa3 (LoA3)
as new Authentication Context Request (ACR) classes.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
LoA2: authentication mechanism using a single factor;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
LoA3: authentication mechanism using multiple authentication factors.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
The following guidance must be observed for the authentication mechanism of Open Finance Brasil APIs:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
In accordance with Art. 17 of Joint Resolution no. 01, institutions must adopt procedures and controls for client authentication compatible with those applicable to access to their electronic service channels.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
In accordance with the regulation in force, it is suggested that:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
For user authentication in authorisations to access data sharing APIs, Authorization Servers should adopt, at least, a method compatible with LoA2; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
For user authentication in authorisations to access payment initiation or service/product contracting APIs, Authorization Servers should adopt an authentication method compatible with LoA3 or higher.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
In all cases, the adoption of a more rigorous authentication mechanism (LoA3 or higher) is at the discretion of the transmitting/account-holding institution, according to its risk assessment and in a manner compatible with the mechanisms usually employed.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Additional clarification on authentication factors[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Authentication factors are:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Something you know, such as a password or secret phrase;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Something you have, such as a token, smartcard or device;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Something you are, that is, authentication conditioned on the presentation of a physical characteristic that is exclusively yours, such as biometric validation.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
To perform multi-factor authentication (MFA), it is necessary that the user presents at least two different factors from those listed above. A single factor used more than once – for example, presenting two passwords that the user knows – cannot be accepted as MFA.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

. This means that the sub is an identifier that is never transferred or changed for the end user within the issuer (account-holding/transmitting institution).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

The Brazilian ICP issues RSA x509 certificates only; therefore, for simplicity, this section removes support for EC algorithms and requires that only encryption algorithms recommended by IANA be used.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
JWS standard defined in RFC7515 shall be adopted to ensure integrity and non-repudiation of information processed in sensitive API's (message sign requirement is indicated at API's documentation/swagger), which includes:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Header (JSON Object Signing and Encryption - JOSE Header), which defines the algorithm used and includes information about the public key or certificate that can be used to validate the signature;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Payload (JWS Payload): the content itself as detailed in the API specification;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Digital signature (JWS Signature): digital signature, performed according to the header parameters.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Each of the elements above must be encoded using the Base64url pattern
RFC4648
and, once this is done, the elements must be concatenated with "." (JWS Compact Serialization method, as defined in
RFC7515
).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
The payload of signed messages (request JWT and response JWT) shall include the following claims as defined in
RFC7519
:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
aud (in the JWT request): the Resource Provider (e.g. the institution holding the account) must validate whether the value of the aud field matches the endpoint being triggered;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
aud (in the JWT response): the API client (e.g. initiating institution) shall validate whether the value of the aud field matches its own organisationId listed in the directory;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
iss (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the receiver of the message shall validate whether the value of the iss field matches the organisationId of the sender;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
jti (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the value of the jti field shall be filled with the UUID defined by the institution in accordance with [RFC4122] using version 4;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
iat (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the value of the iat field shall be filled with the message generation time and in accordance with the standard established in
RFC7519
for the NumericDate format.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
cty (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the value of the cty field shall be filled in; in the normal case in which nested signing or encryption operations are not employed, the use of this header parameter is not recommended. In the case that nested signing or encryption is employed, this header parameter must be present; in this case, the value must be "JWT", to indicate that a nested JWT is carried in this JWT. While media type names are not case sensitive, it is recommended that "JWT" always be spelled using uppercase characters for compatibility with legacy implementations.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
The HTTP content-type of requests and responses with JWS messages shall be defined as: "application/jwt".[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
The JOSE header must contain the following attributes:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
alg - shall be filled with the value PS256";[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
kid - shall be filled with the key identifier value used for the signature;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
typ - shall be filled with the value JWT.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
In case of error in signature validation by Resource Provider the API provider shall return HTTP error message with status code 400 and the ResponseError content shall include, in the code property, the content BAD_SIGNATURE.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Errors in validating the signed messages received by the client application (e.g. payment initiator) must be logged and the Resource Provider (e.g. account-holding institution) must be notified.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
The receiver shall validate the consistency of the JWS message's digital signature exclusively based on the information obtained from the directory, that is, based on the keys published in the institution's JWKS in the directory.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Signatures must be performed using the digital signature certificate specified in the
Open Finance Brazil Certificates Standard
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
the iat claim must be numeric in Unix Time format GMT+0 with a tolerance of +/- 60 seconds;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
the jti claim must be unique for a clientId within a time frame of 86,400 seconds (24h), and cannot be reused within this period. In case of reuse, the HTTP error code 403 shall be return. Any other case must follow RFC 6749 instructions in item 5.2.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
For JWS, both clients and authorization servers shall use the PS256 algorithm.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
For JWE, both clients and authorization servers shall use RSA-OAEP with A256GCM.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
For TLS, Authentication Server endpoints and Resource Server endpoints used directly by the client:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall support TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall support TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
The "TLS Session Resumption" and "TLS Renegotiation" features shall be disabled.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Existing mechanisms for appropriately managing access to resources defined in
RFC6749
are insufficient to meet the requirements of a modern data sharing ecosystem. Using static scope strings does not provide consumers with sufficient control and granularity to manage data sharing or resource management with third parties. Open Finance Brasil has elected to implement the parameterized scope (
FAPI-LIP
) associated with consent/binding APIs to manage fine-grained access to resources.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
This profile defines OAuth 2.0 dynamic scope "consent" as follows:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
string "consent", "recurring-consent" or "enrollment"; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
delimiter of a colon ":"; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Consent Resource Id returned by a successful creation of the resource to be granted (e.g. consent, recurring-consent, enrollment).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
In addition:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
the Consent Resource Id must include url safe characters only;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
the Consent Resource Id must be namespaced;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
the Consent Resource Id must have the properties of a
nonce
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Due to the characteristics of the Consent Resource Id and for ease of implementation, many institutions choose to use a UUIDv4 key as the Consent Resource Id; however, this is not a rule, and each institution may choose other methods provided that the rules presented above and also those defined in each API specification are respected.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Considering that the transmitting/account-holding institution is Banco Exemplo and that it is using UUIDv4 as the Consent Resource Id, the consents/recurring consents/device bindings created against this institution would have the following format, respectively:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
consent:urn:bancoexemplo:830ce3c6-e9e7-4800-ae93-3e9b29b470f1[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
recurring-consent:urn:bancoexemplo:c9a8a741-39a6-4014-bb75-e05934f9d711[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
enrollment:urn:bancoexemplo:eb093d20-ccc5-4242-a271-6658f6663712[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Consent is a fundamental business object, strongly linked to security artefacts (refresh and access tokens). However, its life cycle must be managed independently through its own state machine. The functional API specifications published by Open Finance Brasil define the state transitions, expected behaviours and error conditions for REST resources protected by this profile, ensuring appropriate control over the consent life cycle.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
The following requirements aim to instruct the behaviour of the Authorization Server (AS) in relation to the consent life cycle, ensuring that authorisation practices are aligned with regulatory expectations and the security of the entire ecosystem.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
In addition to the requirements outlined in Open Finance Brasil security provisions the Authorization Server:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall only issue refresh_tokens when linked to an active and valid consent;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Must not issue refresh_token when consent status is "CONSUMED" (for payment services);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
Must issue an access_token through the grant_type client credentials when consent status is "CONSUMED" (for payment services);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
In an optimised journey, it shall issue refresh_tokens as long as at least one of the linked consents is active and valid.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall only share access to resources when presented access_token linked to an active consent and with the status "AUTHORISED“. For tokens generated with the scope: payments or recurring-payments, the status of the consent will not be validated.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
In the scenario of receiving an invalid token, status code 401 should be returned.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall revoke refresh tokens and, access tokens where aplicable, when the linked Consent Resource is deleted;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
In an optimised journey, it shall perform the revocation of refresh_tokens and access_tokens only if both linked consents are revoked.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall ensure access tokens are issued with sufficient scope necessary for access to data specified in the Permission element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall not reject an authorisation request requesting scopes broader than those necessary to access data specified in the Permissions element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
may reduce requested scope to a level sufficient to enable access to data resources specified in the Permissions element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall retain records on the consent history to allow the appropriate formation of audit trails in accordance with the regulation in force;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall return authentication failure and the return code access_denied in the error parameter (as specified in section 4.1.2.1 of
RFC6749
) if the CPF of the authenticated user is not the same as indicated in the loggedUser element of the related Consent Resource Object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall return authentication failure and the return code access_denied in the error parameter (as specified in section 4.1.2.1 of
RFC6749
) if the businessEntity element has not been populated in the related Consent Resource Object and the user has selected or authenticated using credentials related to a legal entity (business) account;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall condition the authentication or selection of legal entity (business) accounts to the consistency between the CNPJ related to the account(s) and the value present in the businessEntity element of the Consent Resource Object. In case of divergence, it shall return authentication failure and the return code access_denied in the error parameter (as specified in section 4.1.2.1 of
RFC6749
);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall issue a refresh_token with a validity period not shorter than the validity of the consent to which it is related, while respecting the other criteria above.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
In addition to the requirements outlined in Open Finance Brasil security provisions, the Confidential Client[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall revoke where possible and cease usage of refresh and access tokens that are bound to a Consent Resource that has been deleted;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0
shall delete Consent Resource that are expired.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.2.0

que fornece diretrizes de implementação específicas para segurança e interoperabilidade que devem ser aplicadas as APIs expostas no ecossistema do Open Finance Brasil. O Perfil de Segurança do Open Finance Brasil é um subconjunto do perfil

FAPI-1-Advanced

o requisito de concessão de acesso granular a recursos, com vistas à minimização de dados;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
o requisito de informar sobre o contexto da autenticação do usuário (claim Authentication Context Request - acr) que foi realizada por um Provedor OpenID, com vistas a favorecer o adequado gerenciamento do risco decorrente do acesso do usuário;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Este perfil também especifica o método para os aplicativos:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
obterem de maneira segura os tokens OAuth necessários para acesso a dados críticos de acordo com os requisitos do
Open Finance Brasil

Para realizar autenticação por múltiplos fatores (MFA) é necessário que o usuário apresente, ao menos, dois diferentes fatores dos listados acima. Um mesmo fator usado mais de uma vez - por exemplo, a apresentação de suas senhas que ele conhece - não pode ser aceito como MFA.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0

No ecossistema do Open Finance Brasil, clientes confidenciais são cliente que foram criados através do DCR (Dynamic Client Registration). RFC7519

No caso de assinatura aninhada ou criptografia ser empregada, este parâmetro de cabeçalho deve estar presente; neste caso, o valor deve ser "JWT", para indicar que um JWT aninhado é transportado neste JWT. Embora os nomes dos tipos de mídia não diferenciem maiúsculas de minúsculas, é recomendável que "JWT" sempre seja escrito com caracteres maiúsculos para compatibilidade com implementações herdadas.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0

Os mecanismos existentes para gerenciar adequadamente o acesso aos recursos definidos em
RFC6749
são insuficientes para atender aos requisitos de um ecossistema de compartilhamento de dados moderno. Utilizar strings de escopo estático não fornece aos consumidores controle de granularidade suficiente para controlar o compartilhamento de dados ou gerenciamento de recursos com terceiros. O Open Finance Brasil optou por implementar o escopo parametrizável (
FAPI-LIP
) associado a APIs de consentimento/vínculo para gerenciar o acesso granular aos recursos.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Este perfil define o escopo dinâmico do OAuth 2.0 da seguinte maneira:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
string “
consent
”, “
recurring-consent
” ou “enrollment”; e[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
delimitador de dois pontos “:”; e[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Consent Resource Id retornado por uma criação bem-sucedida do recurso a ser concedido (ex: consent, recurring-consent, enrollment)[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
O Consent Resource Id:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
deve incluir caracteres seguros para url;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
deve ser “namespaced”;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0

Devido as características do Consent Resource ID e por facilidade de implementação, muitas instituições optam por utilizar uma chave UUIDv4 como Consent Resource ID, no entanto isso não é uma regra e cada instituição pode optar por outros métodos desde que sejam respeitadas as regras acima apresentadas e também definidas nas especificações de cada API.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Considerando que a instituição transmissora/detentora seja o Banco Exemplo e que a mesma esteja utilizando UUIDv4 como Consent Resource ID, os consentimentos/consentimentos recorrentes/vínculos de dispositivo criados contra esta instituição teriam o seguinte formato, respectivamente:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0

O consentimento é um objeto de negócio fundamental, fortemente vinculado aos artefatos de segurança (refresh e access tokens). No entanto, seu ciclo de vida deve ser gerenciado de forma independente, através de sua própria máquina de estados. As especificações funcionais da API publicadas pelo Open Finance Brasil definem as transições de estado, os comportamentos esperados e as condições de erro dos recursos REST protegidos por este perfil, garantindo o controle adequado sobre o ciclo de vida do consentimento.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Os requisitos a seguir visam instruir sobre o comportamento do Servidor de Autorização (AS) em relação ao ciclo de vida do consentimento, assegurando que as práticas de autorização estejam alinhadas com as expectativas normativas e a segurança de todo o ecossistema.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Além dos requisitos descritos nas disposições de segurança do Open Finance Brasil, o Servidor de Autorização[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
deve apenas emitir refresh_tokens quando vinculados a um consentimento ativo e válido;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Não deve emitir refresh_token quando o consentimento estiver no status “CONSUMED” (para serviços de pagamentos);[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Deve emitir um access_token por meio de um grant_type do tipo client credentials no status “CONSUMED” (para serviços de pagamentos).[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Em uma jornada otimizada, deve emitir refresh_tokens enquanto ao menos um dos consentimentos vinculados estiver ativo e válido.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
só deve compartilhar o acesso aos recursos quando apresentado access_token vinculado a um consentimento ativo e com o status "AUTHORISED“. Para tokens gerados com o scope: payments ou recurring-payments
, o
status do consentimento não será validado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
No cenário de recebimento de token inválido, deve ser retornado status code 401.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
deve revogar os refresh tokens e, quando aplicável, os access tokens quando o Consentimento (Consent Resource) relacionado for apagado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Em uma jornada otimizada, deve realizar a revogação dos refresh_tokens e access_tokens apenas se ambos os consentimentos vinculados forem revogados.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
deve garantir que os access tokens são emitidos com os scopes necessários para permitir acesso aos dados especificados em elemento Permission do Consentimento (Consent Resource Object) relacionado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
não deve rejeitar pedido de autorização com scopes além do necessário para permitir acesso a dados definidos em elemento Permission do Consentimento (Consent Resource Object) relacionado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
pode reduzir o escopo solicitado para um nível que seja suficiente para permitir o acesso aos dados definidos em elemento Permission do Consentimento (Consent Resource Object) relacionado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
deve manter registros sobre o histórico dos consentimento para permitir a adequada formação de trilhas de auditoria em conformidade com a regulação em vigor;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
deve retornar falha na autenticação e o código de retorno access_denied no parâmetro erro (como especificado na seção 4.1.2.1 da
RFC6749
) caso o CPF do usuário autenticado não seja o mesmo indicado no elemento loggedUser do Consentimento (Consent Resource Object);[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
deve retornar falha na autenticação e o código de retorno access_denied no parâmetro erro (como especificado na seção 4.1.2.1 da
RFC6749
) caso o elemento businessEntity não tenha sido preenchido no Consentimento (Consent Resource Object) relacionado e o usuário tenha selecionado ou se autenticado por meio de credencial relacionada à conta do tipo Pessoa Jurídica (PJ);[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
deve condicionar a autenticação ou seleção de contas do tipo PJ à consistência entre o CNPJ relacionado à(s) conta(s) e o valor presente no elemento businessEntity do Consentimento (Consent Resource Object). Em caso de divergência deve retornar falha na autenticação e o código de retorno
access_denied
no parâmetro erro (como especificado na seção 4.1.2.1 da
RFC6749

deve emitir

com validade não inferior à validade do consentimento ao qual está relacionado, respeitado os demais critérios acima.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0

The Open Finance Brasil Security Profile (FAPI-BR) consists of the following parts:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0

The Open Finance Brasil Security Profile is an implementation of the
FAPI-1-Advanced
profile that provides specific implementation guidelines for security and interoperability that shall be applied to APIs exposed in the Open Finance Brasil ecosystem. The Open Finance Brasil Security Profile is a subset of the
FAPI-1-Advanced
; however, this subset does not refer to the removal of security mechanisms from the original profile, but rather to the mandatory use of certain characteristics of that profile in order to facilitate interoperability among financial institutions.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
This profile describes the capabilities and security features that shall be provided by servers and clients that are necessary for the Open Finance Brasil ecosystem, defining measures to mitigate or address:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
attacks that address privacy considerations identified in clause 9.1 of
FAPI-1-Advanced
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
the requirement to support fine-grained access to resources, for data minimisation purposes;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
the requirement to convey the Authentication Context Request (acr claim) that was performed by an OpenID Provider, in order to enable appropriate risk management arising from user access.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
This profile also specifies the method for applications to:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
obtain the OAuth tokens in an appropriately secure manner for access to critical data in a manner that meets the requirements of
Open Finance Brasil
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
use OpenID Connect to identify the Open Finance user; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
use OpenID Connect to assert the identity of the client.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Although it is possible to code from scratch an Authorization Server that complies with the Open Finance Brasil Security Profile, the target audience of this specification is providers that already have a certified implementation of
FAPI-1-Advanced
and wish to make the necessary adjustments to obtain certification for the Open Finance Brasil Security Profile.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
