To address the privacy considerations identified in Open Finance Brasil, which were not fully addressed in the final
FAPI-1-Advanced
specification, and to support client management in the Open Finance Brasil ecosystem, the Open Finance Brasil Security Profile establishes that the Authorization Server shall support the provisions specified in clause 5.2.2 of
FAPI-1-Advanced
.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In addition, the Authorization Server shall:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall perform client authentication using private_key_jwt;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall require Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall publish discovery metadata (including the authorization endpoint) via the metadata document as specified in
OIDC-Discovery
and
RFC8414
(".well-known");[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support the claims parameter as defined in clause 5.5 of
OIDC-Core
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support the acr value "urn:brasil:openbanking:loa2" as defined in clause 5.1.1.1;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
should support the acr value "urn:brasil:openbanking:loa3" as defined in clause 5.1.1.1;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall implement the userinfo endpoint as defined in clause 5.3 of
OIDC-Core
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support the parameterized scope as defined in clause 6.3.1 of
FAPI-LIP
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
may support
FAPI-CIBA
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support refresh tokens;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall issue access tokens with an expiry time between 300 seconds (minimum) and 900 seconds (maximum);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support the response_type value "code id_token";[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall not allow refresh token rotation;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall ensure that, in case of sharing the Authorization Server for other services, in addition to Open Finance, it does not disclose and/or allow the use of non-certified methods in the Open Finance environment;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall ensure that the settings disclosed to other participants through OpenID Discovery (indicated by the Well-Known file registered in the Directory) are restricted to the operating modes to which the institution has certified;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall refuse requests, for the Open Finance environment, that are outside the modes of operation to which the institution has certified its Authorization Server;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
the minimum expiration time of request_uri must be 60 seconds;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall refuse requests that do not present the x-fapi-interaction-id header on protected resource endpoints;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall require the use of Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall require the use of subject_type "public";[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall require the use of response_mode "fragment";[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall issue refresh_tokens (JWT or opaque) with no expiration time in scenarios where they are required.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The Authorization Server shall support the provisions specified in clause 5.2.2.1 of
FAPI-1-Advanced
and, in addition, in order to meet specific requirements of the Open Finance Brasil Security Profile, it shall:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall encrypt the id_token in callback and token endpoint calls;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
for the encryption of the id_token, a key of type "enc" available in the JWKS informed in the jwks_uri parameter of the client registration (DCR) must be used. The kid of the key used for the id_token encryption must be indicated in the kid attribute of the JWT header;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall always include the acr claim in the id_token. The value of the acr claim must be one of the allowed values as defined in the section Authentication contexts (acr);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The use of other headers to indicate the key used, such as x5u, x5c, jku or jkw, is prohibited as defined in clause 2 of
OIDC-Core
.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
This profile defines
urn:brasil:openbanking:loa2 (LoA2)
and
urn:brasil:openbanking:loa3 (LoA3)
as new Authentication Context Request (ACR) classes.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
LoA2: authentication mechanism using a single factor;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
LoA3: authentication mechanism using multiple authentication factors.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The following guidance must be observed for the authentication mechanism of Open Finance Brasil APIs:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In accordance with Art. 17 of Joint Resolution no. 01, institutions must adopt procedures and controls for client authentication compatible with those applicable to access to their electronic service channels.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In accordance with the regulation in force, it is suggested that:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
For user authentication in authorisations to access data sharing APIs, Authorization Servers should adopt, at least, a method compatible with LoA2; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
For user authentication in authorisations to access payment initiation or service/product contracting APIs, Authorization Servers should adopt an authentication method compatible with LoA3 or higher.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In all cases, the adoption of a more rigorous authentication mechanism (LoA3 or higher) is at the discretion of the transmitting/account-holding institution, according to its risk assessment and in a manner compatible with the mechanisms usually employed.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Additional clarification on authentication factors[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Authentication factors are:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Something you know, such as a password or secret phrase;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Something you have, such as a token, smartcard or device;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Something you are, that is, authentication conditioned on the presentation of a physical characteristic that is exclusively yours, such as biometric validation.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
To perform multi-factor authentication (MFA), it is necessary that the user presents at least two different factors from those listed above. A single factor used more than once – for example, presenting two passwords that the user knows – cannot be accepted as MFA.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
This profile uses the official definition found at:
Analise requisitos de criptografia ID_TOKEN
. This means that the sub is an identifier that is never transferred or changed for the end user within the issuer (account-holding/transmitting institution).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The authorization server shall mandatorily declare the scopes below in its well-known endpoint, regardless of whether the institution provides the products related to the scopes listed below:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
invoice-financings[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
financings[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
loans[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
unarranged-accounts-overdraft[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
bank-fixed-incomes[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
credit-fixed-incomes[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
variable-incomes[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
treasure-titles[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
funds[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
exchanges[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Scopes not listed above must be declared if the institution provides products related to them (e.g. accounts, payments, etc.).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
A confidential client is any client created through a secure method and that has specific access credentials. In the Open Finance Brasil ecosystem, confidential clients are clients that were created through DCR (Dynamic Client Registration). A confidential client shall support the provisions specified in clause 5.2.3 of
FAPI-1-Advanced
and, in addition, in order to meet specific requirements of the Open Finance Brasil Security Profile, it shall:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support encrypted request objects;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support
PAR
(pushed authorization requests);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support the parameterized scope as defined in clause 6.3.1 of
FAPI-LIP
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support refresh tokens;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall not populate the acr claim with required values;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall require the acr claim as an essential claim;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support the
private_key_jwt
authentication method;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall not allow the refresh token rotation feature;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall send the
x-fapi-interaction-id
header on FAPI endpoints.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Participants shall support all security considerations specified in clause 8 of
FAPI-1-Advanced
and in the
Manual de Segurança de Banco Central do Brasil
.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The Brazilian ICP issues RSA x509 certificates only; therefore, for simplicity, this section removes support for EC algorithms and requires that only encryption algorithms recommended by IANA be used.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
JWS standard defined in RFC7515 shall be adopted to ensure integrity and non-repudiation of information processed in sensitive API's (message sign requirement is indicated at API's documentation/swagger), which includes:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Header (JSON Object Signing and Encryption - JOSE Header), which defines the algorithm used and includes information about the public key or certificate that can be used to validate the signature;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Payload (JWS Payload): the content itself as detailed in the API specification;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Digital signature (JWS Signature): digital signature, performed according to the header parameters.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Each of the elements above must be encoded using the Base64url pattern
RFC4648
and, once this is done, the elements must be concatenated with "." (JWS Compact Serialization method, as defined in
RFC7515
).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The payload of signed messages (request JWT and response JWT) shall include the following claims as defined in
RFC7519
:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
aud (in the JWT request): the Resource Provider (e.g. the institution holding the account) must validate whether the value of the aud field matches the endpoint being triggered;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
aud (in the JWT response): the API client (e.g. initiating institution) shall validate whether the value of the aud field matches its own organisationId listed in the directory;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
iss (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the receiver of the message shall validate whether the value of the iss field matches the organisationId of the sender;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
jti (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the value of the jti field shall be filled with the UUID defined by the institution in accordance with [RFC4122] using version 4;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
iat (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the value of the iat field shall be filled with the message generation time and in accordance with the standard established in
RFC7519
for the NumericDate format.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
cty (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the value of the cty field shall be filled in; in the normal case in which nested signing or encryption operations are not employed, the use of this header parameter is not recommended. In the case that nested signing or encryption is employed, this header parameter must be present; in this case, the value must be "JWT", to indicate that a nested JWT is carried in this JWT. While media type names are not case sensitive, it is recommended that "JWT" always be spelled using uppercase characters for compatibility with legacy implementations.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The HTTP content-type of requests and responses with JWS messages shall be defined as: "application/jwt".[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The JOSE header must contain the following attributes:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
alg - shall be filled with the value PS256";[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
kid - shall be filled with the key identifier value used for the signature;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
typ - shall be filled with the value JWT.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In case of error in signature validation by Resource Provider the API provider shall return HTTP error message with status code 400 and the ResponseError content shall include, in the code property, the content BAD_SIGNATURE.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Errors in validating the signed messages received by the client application (e.g. payment initiator) must be logged and the Resource Provider (e.g. account-holding institution) must be notified.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The receiver shall validate the consistency of the JWS message's digital signature exclusively based on the information obtained from the directory, that is, based on the keys published in the institution's JWKS in the directory.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Signatures must be performed using the digital signature certificate specified in the
Open Finance Brazil Certificates Standard
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
the iat claim must be numeric in Unix Time format GMT+0 with a tolerance of +/- 60 seconds;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
the jti claim must be unique for a clientId within a time frame of 86,400 seconds (24h), and cannot be reused within this period. In case of reuse, the HTTP error code 403 shall be return. Any other case must follow RFC 6749 instructions in item 5.2.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
For JWS, both clients and authorization servers shall use the PS256 algorithm.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
For JWE, both clients and authorization servers shall use RSA-OAEP with A256GCM.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
For TLS, Authentication Server endpoints and Resource Server endpoints used directly by the client:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall support TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The "TLS Session Resumption" and "TLS Renegotiation" features shall be disabled.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Existing mechanisms for appropriately managing access to resources defined in
RFC6749
are insufficient to meet the requirements of a modern data sharing ecosystem. Using static scope strings does not provide consumers with sufficient control and granularity to manage data sharing or resource management with third parties. Open Finance Brasil has elected to implement the parameterized scope (
FAPI-LIP
) associated with consent/binding APIs to manage fine-grained access to resources.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
This profile defines OAuth 2.0 dynamic scope "consent" as follows:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
string "consent", "recurring-consent" or "enrollment"; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
delimiter of a colon ":"; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Consent Resource Id returned by a successful creation of the resource to be granted (e.g. consent, recurring-consent, enrollment).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In addition:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
the Consent Resource Id must include url safe characters only;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
the Consent Resource Id must be namespaced;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
the Consent Resource Id must have the properties of a
nonce
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Due to the characteristics of the Consent Resource Id and for ease of implementation, many institutions choose to use a UUIDv4 key as the Consent Resource Id; however, this is not a rule, and each institution may choose other methods provided that the rules presented above and also those defined in each API specification are respected.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Considering that the transmitting/account-holding institution is Banco Exemplo and that it is using UUIDv4 as the Consent Resource Id, the consents/recurring consents/device bindings created against this institution would have the following format, respectively:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
consent:urn:bancoexemplo:830ce3c6-e9e7-4800-ae93-3e9b29b470f1[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
recurring-consent:urn:bancoexemplo:c9a8a741-39a6-4014-bb75-e05934f9d711[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
enrollment:urn:bancoexemplo:eb093d20-ccc5-4242-a271-6658f6663712[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Consent is a fundamental business object, strongly linked to security artefacts (refresh and access tokens). However, its life cycle must be managed independently through its own state machine. The functional API specifications published by Open Finance Brasil define the state transitions, expected behaviours and error conditions for REST resources protected by this profile, ensuring appropriate control over the consent life cycle.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
The following requirements aim to instruct the behaviour of the Authorization Server (AS) in relation to the consent life cycle, ensuring that authorisation practices are aligned with regulatory expectations and the security of the entire ecosystem.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In addition to the requirements outlined in Open Finance Brasil security provisions the Authorization Server:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall only issue refresh_tokens when linked to an active and valid consent;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Must not issue refresh_token when consent status is "CONSUMED" (for payment services);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
Must issue an access_token through the grant_type client credentials when consent status is "CONSUMED" (for payment services);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In an optimised journey, it shall issue refresh_tokens as long as at least one of the linked consents is active and valid.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall only share access to resources when presented access_token linked to an active consent and with the status "AUTHORISED“. For tokens generated with the scope: payments or recurring-payments, the status of the consent will not be validated.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In the scenario of receiving an invalid token, status code 401 should be returned.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall revoke refresh tokens and, access tokens where aplicable, when the linked Consent Resource is deleted;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In an optimised journey, it shall perform the revocation of refresh_tokens and access_tokens only if both linked consents are revoked.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall ensure access tokens are issued with sufficient scope necessary for access to data specified in the Permission element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall not reject an authorisation request requesting scopes broader than those necessary to access data specified in the Permissions element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
may reduce requested scope to a level sufficient to enable access to data resources specified in the Permissions element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall retain records on the consent history to allow the appropriate formation of audit trails in accordance with the regulation in force;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall return authentication failure and the return code access_denied in the error parameter (as specified in section 4.1.2.1 of
RFC6749
) if the CPF of the authenticated user is not the same as indicated in the loggedUser element of the related Consent Resource Object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall return authentication failure and the return code access_denied in the error parameter (as specified in section 4.1.2.1 of
RFC6749
) if the businessEntity element has not been populated in the related Consent Resource Object and the user has selected or authenticated using credentials related to a legal entity (business) account;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall condition the authentication or selection of legal entity (business) accounts to the consistency between the CNPJ related to the account(s) and the value present in the businessEntity element of the Consent Resource Object. In case of divergence, it shall return authentication failure and the return code access_denied in the error parameter (as specified in section 4.1.2.1 of
RFC6749
);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall issue a refresh_token with a validity period not shorter than the validity of the consent to which it is related, while respecting the other criteria above.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
In addition to the requirements outlined in Open Finance Brasil security provisions, the Confidential Client[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall revoke where possible and cease usage of refresh and access tokens that are bound to a Consent Resource that has been deleted;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0
shall delete Consent Resource that are expired;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile - v2.1.0

A Estrutura Inicial do Open Finance Brasil (EIOFB) é responsável por criar padrões e especificações necessárias para atender aos requisitos e obrigações da Legislação do Open Finance do Brasil, conforme originalmente delineado pelo
Banco Central do Brasil
. É possível que alguns dos elementos deste documento estejam sujeitos a direitos autorais ou patenteados. O EIOFB não se responsabiliza pela identificação de qualquer ou todos esses direitos.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
O Financial-grade API 1.0 do Open Finance Brasil consiste nas seguintes partes:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
¶[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Open Finance Brasil Dynamic Client Registration Profile 1.0[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

RFC6749

OIDC

FAPI-1-Baseline

FAPI-1-Advanced[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
A Financial-grade API do Open Finance Brasil é um perfil OAuth altamente seguro que visa fornecer diretrizes de implementação específicas para segurança e interoperabilidade que podem ser aplicadas a APIs na área de Open Finance do Brasil que requerem um nível de privacidade superior ao fornecido pelo padrão
Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 - Part 2: Advanced
. Entre outras melhorias, esta especificação aborda considerações de privacidade identificadas em
FAPI-1-Advanced
que são relevantes nas especificações do Open Finance Brasil, mas não foram, até agora, exigidas por outras jurisdições.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Embora seja possível codificar um provedor de OpenID e parte de confiança a partir dos primeiros princípios usando esta especificação, o público principal para esta especificação são as partes que já possuem uma implementação certificada do
Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 - Part 2: Advanced
e deseja obter a certificação para o programa Brasil Open Finance.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
As palavras-chave "deve" (shall), "não deve" (shall not), "deveria" (should), "não deveria" (should not) e "pode" (may) presentes nesse documento devem ser interpretadas conforme as diretrizes descritas em
ISO Directive Part 2
observando seguinte equivalência:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
"deve" => equivalente ao termo "shall" e expressa um requerimento definido no documento (nas traduções é similar ao termo "must", que pode denotar um requerimento externo ao documento);[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
"não deve" => equivalente ao termo "shall not" e também expressa um requerimento definido no documento;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
"deveria" e "não deveria"=> equivalente ao termo "should" e "should not" e expressa uma recomendação[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
"pode" => equivalente ao termo "may" indica uma permissão[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Estas palavras-chave não são usadas como termos de dicionário, de modo que qualquer ocorrência deles deve ser interpretada como palavras-chave e não devem ser interpretados com seus significados de linguagem natural.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

O perfil de segurança do Open Finance Brasil especifica requisitos adicionais de segurança e de identificação para o acesso a API's com recursos críticos protegidas pelo OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, que consiste em
RFC6749
,
RFC6750
,
RFC7636
,
FAPI-1-Baseline
,
FAPI-1-Advanced
e outras especificações.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Este perfil descreve as capacidades e os recursos de segurança que devem ser oferecidos por servidores e clientes que são necessários para o Programa do Open Finance Brasil, definindo as medidas para mitigar ou endereçar:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
ataques que abordam considerações de privacidade identificadas na cláusula 9.1 de [FAPI-1 Advanced].[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
o requisito de concessão de acesso granular a recursos, com vistas à minimização de dados;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
o requisito de informar sobre o contexto da autenticação do usuário (claim Authentication Context Request - acr) que foi realizada por um Provedor OpenID, com vistas a favorecer o adequado gerenciamento do risco decorrente do acesso do usuário;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
O Open Finance Brasil tem um requisito para endereçar considerações de privacidade que foram identificadas, mas não abordadas na especificação final
FAPI-1-Advanced
, sem impor requisitos adicionais aos Servidores de Autorização que estão sendo propostos em
FAPI-2-Baseline
.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Este perfil descreve os requisitos de gerenciamento de clientes necessários para dar suporte ao ecossistema Open Finance Brasil mais amplo.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Como um perfil do OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, este documento exige o seguinte para o perfil de segurança do Open Finance Brasil.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
O Servidor de Autorização deve suportar as disposições especificadas na cláusula 5.2.2 de
Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 - Parte 2: Advanced
.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Além disso, ele deve:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve realizar a autenticação do cliente utilizando private_key_jwt;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve exigir requisições do tipo "pushed authorization requests" PAR;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

OIDD
e [RFC8414] (".well-known");[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve suportar os parâmetros claims como definido no item 5.5 do
OpenID Connect Core

deve suportar o atributo acr "urn:brasil:openbanking:loa2" como definido no item 5.2.2.3;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deveria suportar o atributo acr "urn:brasil:openbanking:loa3" como definido no item 5.2.2.3;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

pode suportar

(requisito temporariamente retirado);[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve suportar refresh tokens;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve emitir access tokens com o tempo de expiração entre 300 (mínimo) e 900 (máximo) segundos;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve sempre incluir a claim acr no id_token;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve suportar os valores code e id_token para o atributo response_type;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
não deve permitir o recurso de rotação de refresh tokens;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve garantir que em caso de compartilhamento do Servidor de Autorização para outros serviços, além do Open Finance, não divulgue e/ou possibilite o uso de métodos não certificados no ambiente do Open Finance;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve garantir que as configurações divulgadas aos demais participantes através do OpenID Discovery (indicado pelo arquivo de Well-Known cadastrado no Diretório) sejam restritos aos modos de operação aos quais a instituição se certificou;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

deve recusar requisições, para o ambiente do Open Finance, que estejam fora dos modos de operação ao qual a instituição certificou seu Servidor de Autorização;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 - Parte 2: Advanced[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Deve obrigatoriamente criptografar o id_token nos momentos de call-back e chamada do endpoint de token;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Para a criptografia do id_token deve ser utilizada chave disponível no JWKS informado no parâmetro jwks_uri, com o atributo “use”:”enc”, durante o registro do cliente, indicada através do cabeçalho kid do documento JWT;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

OIDC

Este perfil usa a definição oficial encontrada em: Analise requisitos de criptografia ID_TOKEN. Isso significa que o sub é um identificador nunca transferido ou alterado para o usuário final dentro da emissora (detentora/transmissora).[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Esse perfil define "urn:brasil:openbanking:loa2" e "urn:brasil:openbanking:loa3" como novas classes de "Authentication Context Request" (ACR)[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
LoA2: mecanismo de autenticação com a adoção de um único fator[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
LoA3: mecanismo de autenticação com múltiplos fatores de autenticação[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
A seguinte orientação deve ser observada para o mecanismo de autenticação das APIs do Open Finance Brasil:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
De acordo com o Art. 17 da Resolução Conjunta nº 01, as instituições devem adotar procedimentos e controles para autenticação de cliente compatíveis com os aplicáveis ao acesso a seus canais de atendimento eletrônicos.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Em observância à regulação em vigor, sugere-se que:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Para a autenticação do usuário em autorizações de acessos às APIs de compartilhamento de dados (Fase 2), os Authorization Servers deveriam adotar, no mínimo, método compatível com LoA2; e[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Para a autenticação do usuário em autorizações de acessos às API's das fases subsequentes, os Authorization Servers deveriam adotar método de autenticação compatível com LoA3 ou superior.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Em todos os casos, a adoção de mecanismo de autenticação mais rigoroso (LoA3 ou superior) fica a critério da instituição transmissora ou detentora de conta, de acordo com sua avaliação de riscos e de forma compatível com os mecanismos habitualmente utilizados.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Esclarecimentos adicionais sobre fatores de autenticação[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
São fatores de autenticação:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Aquilo que você conhece, como uma senha ou frase secreta[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Aquilo que você tem, como um token, smartcard ou dispositivo[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Aquilo que "você é", ou seja, autenticação condicionada a apresentação de uma característica física exclusivamente sua, como a validação por biometria[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Para realizar autenticação por múltiplos fatores (MFA) é necessário que o usuário apresente, ao menos, dois diferentes fatores dos listados acima. Um mesmo fator usado mais de uma vez - por exemplo, a apresentação de suas senhas que ele conhece - não pode ser aceito como MFA.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

RFC7519
:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
aud (na requisição JWT): o Provedor do Recurso (p. ex. a instituição detentora da conta) deverá validar se o valor do campo aud coincide com o endpoint sendo acionado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
aud (na resposta JWT): o cliente da API (p. e. instituição iniciadora) deverá validar se o valor do campo aud coincide com o seu próprio organisationId listado no diretório;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
iss (na requisição JWT e na resposta JWT): o receptor da mensagem deverá validar se o valor do campo iss coincide com o organisationId do emissor;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
jti (na requisição JWT e na resposta JWT): o valor do campo jti deverá ser preenchido com o UUID definido pela instituição de acordo com a [RFC4122] usando o versão 4;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
iat (na requisição JWT e na resposta JWT): o valor do campo iat deverá ser preenchido com horário da geração da mensagem e de acordo com o padrão estabelecido na
RFC7519
para o formato NumericDate.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
cty (na requisição JWT e na resposta JWT): o valor do campo cty deverá ser preenchido caso as operações de assinatura ou criptografia aninhadas não sejam empregadas, o uso desse parâmetro de cabeçalho não é recomendado. No caso de assinatura aninhada ou criptografia ser empregada, este parâmetro de cabeçalho deve estar presente; neste caso, o valor deve ser "JWT", para indicar que um JWT aninhado é transportado neste JWT. Embora os nomes dos tipos de mídia não diferenciem maiúsculas de minúsculas, é recomendável que "JWT" sempre seja escrito com caracteres maiúsculos para compatibilidade com implementações herdadas.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
O content-type HTTP das requisições e respostas com mensagens JWS deve ser definido como: "application/jwt".[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
No cabeçalho JOSE deve constar os seguintes atributos:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
alg - deve ser preenchido com o valor PS256";[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
kid - deve ser obrigatoriamente preenchido com o valor do identificador da chave utilizado para a assinatura;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Em caso de erro na validação da assinatura pelo Provedor do Recurso a API deve retornar mensagem de erro HTTP com status code 400 e a resposta deve incluir na propriedade code do objeto de resposta de erro especificado na API (ResponseError) a indicação da falha com o conteúdo BAD_SIGNATURE.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Erros na validação da mensagem recebida pela aplicação cliente (p. ex. iniciador de pagamento) devem ser registrados e o Provedor do Recurso (p. ex. instituição detentora de conta) deve ser notificado.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
O receptor deve validar a consistência da assinatura digital da mensagem JWS exclusivamente com base nas informações obtidas do diretório, ou seja, com base nas chaves publicadas no JWKS da instituição no diretório.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
As assinaturas devem ser realizadas com uso do certificado digital de assinatura especificado no
Padrão de Certificados Open Finance Brasil
;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
A claim iat deve ser numérica no formato Unix Time GMT+0 com tolerância de +/- 60 segundos;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
A claim do jti deve ser única para um clientId dentro de um intervalo de tempo de 86.400 segundos (24h), não podendo ser reutilizada neste período. Em caso de reutilização, deverá ser retornado o código de erro HTTP 403. Demais casos seguir instrução da RFC 6749, item 5.2;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Para JWS, clientes e servidores de autorização[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
devem usar o algoritmo PS256;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Para JWE, clientes e servidores de autorização[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
devem usar RSA-OAEP com A256GCM[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Para TLS, endpoints do Servidor de Autenticação e endpoints do Servidor de Recursos usados diretamente pelo cliente:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
devem suportar TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
devem suportar TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
As funcionalidades "TLS Session Resumption" e "TLS Renegotiation" devem ser desabilitadas[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Os mecanismos existentes para gerenciar adequadamente o acesso aos recursos definidos em
RFC6749
são insuficientes para atender aos requisitos de um ecossistema de compartilhamento de dados moderno. Aproveitar strings de escopo estático não fornece aos consumidores controle de granularidade suficiente para compartilhar com terceiros. O Open Finance Brasil optou por implementar uma
API de consentimento
como um recurso protegido OAuth 2.0 que pode ser usado para gerenciar o acesso granular aos recursos. A referência ao recurso de consentimento será transmitida como parte de um escopo de recurso dinâmico OAuth 2.0.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Este perfil define o escopo dinâmico do OAuth 2.0 "consentimento" da seguinte maneira:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
string 'consent’ ou ‘recurring-consent’; e[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
delimitador de dois pontos ":"; e[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Consent API REST Resource Id retornado por uma criação bem-sucedida de
Open Finance Consent Resource
;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Adicionalmente:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Consent Resource Id deve incluir caracteres seguros para url;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Consent Resource Id deve ser "namespaced";[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Consent Resource Id deve ter propriedades de um nonce
Nonce
;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
consent:urn:bancoex:C1DD33123[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
O recurso de consentimento tem um ciclo de vida gerenciado separada e distintamente da estrutura de autorização OAuth 2.0. As transições de estado e comportamentos esperados e condições de erro esperados dos Recursos REST protegidos com este perfil são definidos nas especificações funcionais da API publicadas pelo Open Finance Brasil.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Além dos requisitos descritos nas disposições de segurança do Open Finance Brasil, o Servidor de Autorização[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve apenas emitir refresh_tokens quando vinculados a um consentimento ativo e válido;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Não deve emitir refresh_token quando o consentimento estiver no status “CONSUMED” (para fase 3);[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Deve emitir um access_token por meio de um grant_type do tipo client credentials no status “CONSUMED” (para fase 3).[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
só deve compartilhar o acesso aos recursos quando apresentado access_token vinculado a um consentimento ativo e com o status "AUTHORISED“. Para tokens gerados com o scope: payments ou recurring-payments
, o
status do consentimento não será validado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
No cenário de recebimento de token inválido, deve ser retornado status code 401.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve revogar os refresh tokens e, quando aplicável, os access tokens quando o Consentimento (Consent Resource) relacionado for apagado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve garantir que os access tokens são emitidos com os scopes necessários para permitir acesso aos dados especificados em elemento Permission do Consentimento (Consent Resource Object) relacionado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
não deve rejeitar pedido de autorização com scopes além do necessário para permitir acesso a dados definidos em elemento Permission do Consentimento (Consent Resource Object) relacionado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
pode reduzir o escopo solicitado para um nível que seja suficiente para permitir o acesso aos dados definidos em elemento Permission do Consentimento (Consent Resource Object) relacionado;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve manter registros sobre o histórico dos consentimento para permitir a adequada formação de trilhas de auditoria em conformidade com a regulação em vigor;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve retornar falha na autenticação e o código de retorno _accessdenied no parâmetro erro (como especificado na seção 4.1.2.1 da
RFC6749
) caso o CPF do usuário autenticado não seja o mesmo indicado no elemento loggedUser do Consentimento (Consent Resource Object);[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve retornar falha na autenticação e o código de retorno _accessdenied no parâmetro erro (como especificado na seção 4.1.2.1 da
RFC6749
) caso o elemento businessEntity não tenha sido preenchido no Consentimento (Consent Resource Object) relacionado e o usuário tenha selecionado ou se autenticado por meio de credencial relacionada à conta do tipo Pessoa Jurídica (PJ);[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve condicionar a autenticação ou seleção de contas do tipo PJ à consistência entre o CNPJ relacionado à(s) conta(s) e o valor presente no elemento businessEntity do Consentimento (Consent Resource Object). Em caso de divergência deve retornar falha na autenticação e o código de retorno
access_denied
no parâmetro erro (como especificado na seção 4.1.2.1 da
RFC6749
);[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve emitir
refresh_token
com validade não inferior à validade do consentimento ao qual está relacionado, respeitado os demais critérios acima.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Além dos requisitos descritos nas disposições de segurança do Open Finance Brasil, o Cliente Confidencial[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve, sempre que possível, revogar e cessar o uso de refresh e de access tokens vinculados a um consentimento (Consent Resource Object) que foi excluído;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
deve excluir consentimentos (Consent Resource Objects) que estão expirados;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

The Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API is a highly secured OAuth profile that aims to provide specific implementation guidelines for security and interoperability which can be applied to APIs in the Brasil Open Finance area that require a higher level of privacy than provided by standard
Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 - Part 2: Advanced
. Among other enhancements, this specification addresses privacy considerations identified in
FAPI-1-Advanced
that are relevent in the Open Finance Brasil specifications but have not, so far, been required by other jurisdictions.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 - Part 2: Advanced
and want to achieve certification for the Brasil Open Finance programme.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

shall issue access tokens with an expiry no greater than 900 seconds and no less than 300 seconds;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall always include an acr claim in the id_token;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall support the response_type value code id_token;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall not allow refresh token rotation;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall ensure that, in case of sharing the Authorization Server for other services, in addition to Open Finance, it does not disclose and/or allow the use of non-certified methods in the Open Finance environment;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall ensure that the settings disclosed to other participants through OpenID Discovery (indicated by the Well-Known file registered in the Directory) are restricted to the operating modes to which the institution has certified;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall keep in your settings the methods for which there are still active clients;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall update the records that use non-certified methods, through bilateral treatment between the institutions involved;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall refuse requests, for the Open Finance environment, that are outside the modes of operation to which the institution has certified its Authorization Server;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
the minimum expiration time of request_uri must be 60 seconds;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall deny all requests without header x-fapi-interaction-id on protected resources endpoints;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
must require the use of Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
must require the use of subject_type “
public
”;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
must require the use of response_mode “fragment”;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall issue refresh_tokens (JWT or opaque) without an expiration period in scenarios where it is necessary.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
The Authorization Server shall support the provisions specified in clause 5.2.2.1 of
Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 - Part 2: Advanced[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Shall encrypt the id_token in callback and token endpoint;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
For the encryption of the id_token, a key available in the JWKS informed in the jwks_uri parameter, with the attribute “use”:”enc”, during the client registration must be used, indicated through the kid header of the JWT document;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

The following rules are applicable to the authentication mechanism of Open Finance Brazil API's:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
In accordance to Art. 17 of
Joint Resolution nº 01 - Open Banking Brasil
, institutions must adopt procedures and controls for client authentication compatible with those applicable in their electronic service channels.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
In accordance with the regulation, it is suggested that:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
For Read-Only APIs (Phase 2): the Authorization Servers should adopt, at least, an authentication method compatible with LoA2; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
For Read-Write API's (subsequent phases): the Authorization Servers should adopt an authentication method compatible with LoA3 or higher.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
In all cases, the adoption of a more rigorous authentication mechanism (LoA3 or higher) is at the discretion of the Bank (ASPSP), according to its risk assessment and in a manner compatible with the mechanisms usually employed.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Authentication factors clarification[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
The authentication methods are:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Something you know, such as password or phrase[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Something you have, such as token, smartcard or device[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Something you are, meaning an authentication that makes use of physical characteristics, such as biometric validation.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
To performe a MFA authentication is necessary that the end user presents at least two different methods as listed above. A unique method used more than once - ie. presenting passwords - is not accepted as MFA.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

JWS standad defined in
RFC7515
shall be adopted to ensure integrity and non-repudiation of information processed in sensitive API's (message sign requirement is indicated at API's documentation/swagger), which includes:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Header (JSON Object Signing and Encryption - JOSE Header), which defines the algorithm used and includes information about the public key or certificate that can be used to validate the signature;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Payload (JWS Payload): content itself as detailed in the API specification;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Digital signature (JWS Signature): digital signature, performed according to header parameters.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Each of elements above must be encoded using the Base64url pattern
RFC4648
and the elements must be concatenated with "." (JWS Compact Serialization method as defined in
RFC7515
).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
The payload of signed messages (request JWT and response JWT) shall include the following claims as defined at
RFC7519
:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
aud (in the JWT request): the Resource Provider (eg the institution holding the account) must validate if the value of the aud field matches the endpoint being triggered;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
aud (in JWT response): the API client (eg initiating institution) shall validate if the value of the aud field matches its own organisationId listed in the directory;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
iss (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the receiver of the message shall validate if the value of the iss field matches the organisationId of the sender;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
jti (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the value of the jti field shall be filled with the UUID defined by the institution according to [RFC4122] version 4;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
iat (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the iat field shall be filled with the message generation time and according to the standard established in RFC7519 to the NumericDate format.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
cty (in the JWT request and in the JWT response): the cty field shall be filled in the normal case in which nested signing or encryption operations are not employed, the use of this Header Parameter is not recommended. In the case that nested signing or encryption is employed, this Header Parameter must be present; in this case, the value must be "JWT", to indicate that a Nested JWT is carried in this JWT. While media type names are not case sensitive, it is recommended that "JWT" always be spelled using uppercase characters for compatibility with legacy implementations.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
The HTTP content-type of requests and responses with JWS messages shall be defined as: "application/jwt".[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
The JOSE header must contain the following attributes:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
alg - shall be filled with the value PS256";[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
kid - shall be filled with the key identifier value used for the signature;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
In case of error in signature validation by Resource Provider the API provider shall return HTTP error message with status code 400 and the ResponseError content shall include, in the code property, the content BAD_SIGNATURE.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Errors in validating the signed messages received by the client application (eg payment initiator) must be logged and the Resource Provider (eg account holding institution) must be notified.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
The receiver shall validate the consistency of the JWS message's digital signature exclusively based on the information obtained from the directory, that is, based on the keys published in the institution's JWKS in the directory.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Signatures must be performed using the digital signature certificate specified in the
Open Finance Brazil Certificates Standard
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
the iat claim must be numeric in Unix Time format GMT+0 with a tolerance of +/- 60 seconds;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
the jti claim must be unique for a clientId within a time frame of 86,400 seconds (24h), and cannot be reused within this period. In case of reuse, the HTTP error code 403 shall be return. Any other case must follow RFC 6749 instructions in item 5.2.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
For JWS, both clients and Authorization Servers[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall use PS256 algorithm;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
For JWE, both clients and Authorization Servers[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

Existing mechanisms for appropriately managing access to resources defined in
RFC6749
are insufficient to meet the requirements for a modern data sharing ecosystem. Leveraging static scope strings does not provide consumers control of sufficient granularity to share with third parties. Open Finance Brasil have elected to implement a
Consent API
as a OAuth 2.0 protected resource that can be used to manage fine grain access to resources. The reference to the Consent Resource will be conveyed as part of an OAuth 2.0 dynamic resource scope.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
This profile defines OAuth 2.0 dynamic scope "consent" as follows:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
string 'consent' or ‘recurring-consent’ and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
delimiter of a colon ":"; and[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Consent API REST Resource Id as returned by a successful creation of
Open Finance Consent Resource
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
In addition:[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
the Consent Resource Id must include url safe characters only;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
the Consent Resource Id must be namespaced;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
the Consent Resource Id must have the properties of a nonce
Nonce
;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
consent:urn:bancoex:C1DD33123[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
The Consent Resource has a life cycle that is managed seperately and distinctly from the OAuth 2.0 Authorisation Framework. The state transitions and expected behaviours and error conditions expected of REST Resources protected with this profile are defined in the functional API specifications published by Open Finance Brasil.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
In addition to the requirements outlined in Open Finance Brasil security provisions the Authorization Server[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall only issue refresh_tokens when linked to an active and valid consent;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Must not issue refresh_token when consent status is "CONSUMED" (for phase 3);[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
Must issue an access_token through the grant_type client credentials when consent status is "CONSUMED"(for phase 3).[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall only share access to resources when presented access_token linked to an active consent and with the status "AUTHORISED“. For tokens generated with the scope: payments or recurring-payments, the status of the consent will not be validated.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
In the scenario of receiving an invalid token, status code 401 should be returned.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall revoke refresh tokens and, access tokens where aplicable, when the linked Consent Resource is deleted;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall ensure access tokens are issued with sufficient scope necessary for access to data specified in the Permission element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall not reject an authorisation request requesting scopes broader than those necessary to access data specified in the Permissions element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
may reduce requested scope to a level sufficient to enable access to data resources specified in the Permissions element of a linked Consent Resource object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall retain a complete audit history of the consent resource in accordance with current Central Bank brazilian regulation;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3
shall return authentication failure and return code _accessdenied in the error parameter (as specified in section 4.1.2.1 of
RFC6749
) if the CPF of the authenticated user is not the same as indicated in the loggedUser element of the Consent Resource Object;[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 Implementers Draft 3

RFC6749

RFC6749

https://openfinancebrasil.org.brPeríodo de Convivência - FAPI-BR 2.0 (FAPI-Único)
Apoiar as instituições participantes do Open Finance com orientações para a implementação do perfil FAPI único de segurança, especialmente no período de convivência entre os perfis antigos e o novo que ocorrerá entre 25/03/2024 e 14/04/2024.Período de Convivência - FAPI-BR 2.0 (FAPI-Único)
As especificações de segurança do Open Finance são baseadas no FAPI, da OpenID Foundation, e permitiam que as autenticações fossem realizadas através de oito métodos diferentes, com variantes de Private Key e mTLS, com ou sem PAR, com ou sem JARM. A fim de simplificar a comunicação entre as instituições e melhorar a interoperabilidade, a documentação foi atualizada para criação de um perfil FAPI único que deverá ser implementado por todas as instituições do ecossistema.Período de Convivência - FAPI-BR 2.0 (FAPI-Único)
O cronograma de adequação das instituições prevê um período de três semanas de convivência entre os perfis, para que as iniciadoras de pagamento e receptoras de dados façam os devidos DCMs e ajustes bilaterais com as detentoras de conta e transmissoras de dados, antes da descontinuação dos perfis anteriores. A realização dos DCMs a tempo é necessária para a devida implementação das novas APIs de Consentimento e de Pagamentos.Período de Convivência - FAPI-BR 2.0 (FAPI-Único)

A principal mudança do FAPI-Único é a adoção de um único método de autenticação, o private-key-jwt. Durante o período de convivência é imprescindível que os participantes mantenham disponíveis todos os métodos de autenticação que ofereciam na primeira versão do FAPI-BR.Período de Convivência - FAPI-BR 2.0 (FAPI-Único)
Na primeira versão do FAPI, os servidores de autenticação eram obrigados a oferecer ao menos uma das seguintes opções de métodos de autenticação private-key-jwt ou mtls que poderiam, ainda, ser combinadas com o uso de PAR.Período de Convivência - FAPI-BR 2.0 (FAPI-Único)

A Estrutura Inicial do Open Finance Brasil (EIOFB) é responsável por criar padrões e especificações necessárias para atender aos requisitos e obrigações da Legislação do Open Finance do Brasil, conforme originalmente delineado pelo
Banco Central do Brasil
. É possível que alguns dos elementos deste documento estejam sujeitos a direitos autorais ou patenteados. O EIOFB não se responsabiliza pela identificação de qualquer ou todos esses direitos.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
O Financial-grade API 1.0 do Open Finance Brasil consiste nas seguintes partes:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
Open Finance Brasil Dynamic Client Registration Profile 1.0[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
Estas partes são destinados a serem usados com [RFC6749], [RFC6750], [RFC7636], [OIDC], [FAPI-1-Baseline] e [FAPI-1-Advanced][PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
A Financial-grade API do Open Finance Brasil é um perfil OAuth altamente seguro que visa fornecer diretrizes de implementação específicas para segurança e interoperabilidade que podem ser aplicadas a APIs na área de Open Finance do Brasil que requerem um nível de privacidade superior ao fornecido pelo padrão [Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 - Part 2: Advanced][FAPI-1-Advanced]. Entre outras melhorias, esta especificação aborda considerações de privacidade identificadas em [FAPI-1-Advanced] que são relevantes nas especificações do Open Finance Brasil, mas não foram, até agora, exigidas por outras jurisdições.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
Embora seja possível codificar um provedor de OpenID e parte de confiança a partir dos primeiros princípios usando esta especificação, o público principal para esta especificação são as partes que já possuem uma implementação certificada do [Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 - Part 2: Advanced][FAPI-1-Advanced] e deseja obter a certificação para o programa Brasil Open Finance.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0

Estas palavras-chave não são usadas como termos de dicionário, de modo que qualquer ocorrência deles deve ser interpretada como palavras-chave e não devem ser interpretados com seus significados de linguagem natural.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0

O perfil de segurança do Open Finance Brasil especifica requisitos adicionais de segurança e de  identificação para o acesso a API´s com recursos críticos protegidas pelo OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, que consiste em [RFC6749], [RFC6750], [RFC7636], [FAPI-1-Baseline], [FAPI-1-Advanced] e outras especificações.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
Este perfil descreve as capacidades e os recursos de segurança que devem ser oferecidos por servidores e clientes que são necessários para o Programa do Open Finance Brasil, definindo as medidas para mitigar ou endereçar:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
ataques que abordam considerações de privacidade identificadas na cláusula 9.1 de [FAPI-1 Advanced].[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
o requisito de concessão de acesso granular a recursos, com vistas à minimização de dados;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
o requisito de informar sobre o contexto da autenticação do usuário (claim Authentication Context Request - acr) que foi realizada por um Provedor OpenID, com vistas a favorecer o adequado gerenciamento do risco decorrente do acesso do usuário;[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
o requisito para que os clientes de API declarem um relacionamento prévio com o usuário, afirmando em uma
claim
de identificação do usuário como parte do fluxo de autorização.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
O Open Finance Brasil tem um requisito para endereçar considerações de privacidade que foram identificadas, mas não abordadas na especificação final
FAPI-1-Advanced
, sem impor requisitos adicionais aos Servidores de Autorização que estão sendo propostos em
FAPI-2-Baseline
.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
Os participantes desse ecossistema precisam que os clientes de API solicitem a um provedor openid a confirmação dos valores das
claims
de identificação do usuário como parte de uma solicitação de autorização usando o mecanismo definido na cláusula 5.5.1 de [OIDC].[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
O uso do parâmetro
claims
para solicitar a validação de valores de identificação explícitos requer que os clientes de API protejam com criptografia o Request Object para evitar vazamento de informações. Este risco é identificado na cláusula 7.4.1 do [FAPI-1-Baseline].[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
Além disso, este perfil descreve o escopo específico, valores de
acr
e requisitos de gerenciamento de clientes necessários para dar suporte ao ecossistema Open Finance Brasil mais amplo.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0

Este perfil define "cnpj" como uma nova reivindicação padrão de acordo com cláusula 5.1 [OIDC][PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
CNPJ
, abreviação de Cadastro Nacional de Pessoas Jurídicas, é um número de identificação de empresas
brasileiras
emitidas pelo Ministério da Fazenda
brasileira
,
na
"Secretaria da Receita Federal" ou "Ministério da Fazenda" do Brasil. No modelo de identidade do Open Finance Brasil, pessoas físicas podem se associar a 0 ou mais CNPJs. Um CNPJ é uma string que consiste em números de 14 dígitos e pode começar com 0, os primeiros oito dígitos identificam a empresa, os quatro dígitos após a barra identificam a filial ou subsidiária ("0001" padrão para a sede), e os dois últimos são dígitos de soma de verificação. Para este perfil, o pedido de cnpj deve ser solicitado e fornecido como o número de 14 dígitos.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0

for solicitada como essencial para constar no ID Token ou na resposta ao endpoint UserInfo, o Authorization Server deve incluir no ID Token ou na resposta ao endpoint UserInfo um

relacionado à conta utilizada na autenticação do usuário.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
Se a Claim

indicada como essencial não puder ser preenchida ou validada, o Authorization Server deve tratar a solicitação como uma tentativa de autenticação com falha.[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
Nome: cnpj, Tipo: Array of Strings, Array Element Regex: '^\d{14}$'[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0

São fatores de autenticação:[PT] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
Aquilo que

Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0 - Part 2: Advanced

FAPI-1-Advanced
that are relevent in the Open Finance Brasil specifications but have not, so far, been required by other jurisdictions.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0

and want to achieve certification for the Brasil Open Finance programme.[EN] Open Finance Brasil Financial-grade API Security Profile 1.0
